display_title: Official Review of Paper386 by Reviewer XJTo

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper considers improving the segmentation performance from the view of jointly pre-training a network with multiple segmentation datasets. The paper proposed a series of methods to make the multiple segmentation datasets to be synergistic and obtain obvious improvement proved by comprehensive experiments.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
Overall speaking, the paper proposed a promising solution to further improve the segmentation performance. The author leveraged the vision language model in a smart way to avoid the conflicts caused by different datasets and let them work together and promote each other. Specially, I like the multi-label mapping loss part, which should be emphasized. 

Weakness:
1. The motivation of this paper is not clear to me. I can hardly understand why the 'cat' and 'dog' have so similar language features (shown in Table 1), since a lot of vision-language foundational models, e.g. CLIP, shows terrific performance on zero-shot classification accuracy on ImageNet. If 'cat' and 'dog' have similar embedding, the model should have failed to classify these two classes.

2. I also do not quite understand the role played by the loss L_v. It looks to me that it still pushes features that are from the same class to be together as what the cross-entropy loss does. And why adding L_v can bring further improvement instead of overwhelmed by the multi-label mapping loss?

3. The improvement between jointly train multiple datasets with CE loss in a trivial way and the proposed method seems to be small (71.09 vs 72.6 according to Table 4). I would like the author to provide the results of ADE20k for further analysis. More importantly, I'm curious whether the proposed method can be extended to other segmentation heads with better performance. For instance, I'm curious whether the proposed method can work with mask2former and still bring some improvements compared to the best results obtained by mask2former on ADE20k.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality, clarity and originality is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: See the details of strength and weakness. Generally speaking, the paper has high quality and I would reconsider my rating once I see how well the author addresses my concerns.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Multimodal Supervision pre-training for semantic segmentation. It improves the quality of language embeddings to fit the segmentation model and generates momentum-updated visual embeddings for each category to facilitate better visual representation modelling. Experiments show its advantages over ImageNet pretraining and fine-tuning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1, The motivation is clear, and the writing is easy to follow. 

2, The proposed framework consistently outperforms the pretrained models over ImageNet by a considerable margin under standard fine-tuning.

Weakness:

1, The idea or motivation of using multi-dataset pre-training is not new, as well as using text embedding to replace the one-hot label. Such method is explored in previous works. 

Semantic segmentation from sentences-arxiv.02.2022. 

2, The of technical contribution of this paper has two folds: One introduces the learnable text prompts. The other introduces pixel-text contrasts loss rather than simple CE loss. There are existing approaches in previous works.

1. Learning to prompt for vision language models. IJCV-2022.
2. Exploring cross-image pixel contrast for semantic segmentation-ICCV-2021.

3, The compared baseline and methods are not relevant in Tab.2 including DenseCL, MoCo-V2.  Why not compare the following methods?
Semantic segmentation from sentences-arxiv.02.2022


4, The results are not very significant.

 1, In Tab-4, the improvements from joint Visual + Language supervision are not very significant and even little trivial.

 2, The author should report the results of M-Seg to show scalability of the proposed approach.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on strength and weakness, I give my rating as board line reject mainly due to novelty and significance.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper combines multiple segmentation datasets to train a pre-trained model for semantic segmentation applications. The authors first propose a multi-modal supervision training strategy,  including a language loss and a vision loss. Secondly, a  'cross-modal information exchange' module is presented, which adjusts the ground truth for embedding semantic information. Experimental results show the effectiveness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. This paper proposes a new image segmentation pretraining.
2. The pretraining shows better performance than prior works.

Weaknesses
1. What are 'j', 'T_{j}'  and 'T_{k}' in Eqn (1)?
2. In Eqn (2), what do 'V_{j}' and 'V_{k}' mean?
3. 'M' is ambiguous, which simultaneously represents the number of prompt tokens and the pixel embedding in the memory bank.
4. F also simultaneously represents the visual encoder and the pixel embedding.
5. In Eqn (4), 'V_{j}' is calculated from the previous 'V_{j}^{old}'. So, how to generate the initial 'V_{j}'?
6. What does ' y' ' mean in Eqn (5) and Eqn (6)?
7. The authors do not well explain their equations, especially Eqn (2), Eqn (4), Eqn (5) and Eqn (6). Only a part of variables in these equations are explained. The meaning of the entire equation is not provided.
8. What text encoder do you use? Is it fixed during the training?
9. Fig 2 is very similar to Fig. 1. It can be removed.
10. In Fig. 3, what does each column mean?
11. How do you combine multiple datasets? How do you deal with the same classes in different datasets? How do you deal with the same classes with different names in different datasets (eg, 'airplane' in a dataset and 'aeroplane' in another dataset)?
12. In Table 1&2, please provide the citation of each method.
13. In Table 4, compared with 'CE', the proposed 'Visual + Language' only shows slight improvements.

14. Due to the unclarity of this paper, I cannot fully evaluate the novelty. For the first contribution, the vision loss, I guess it encourages the pixel embeddings of the same class to be similar. For the second contribution, the cross-modal information exchange module, I cannot understand how it works and why it can solve the domain gap problem.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is very hard to read, so readers cannot well understand the novelty and are tough to reproduce. The clarity needs to be further improved.
content.summary_of_the_review: The motivation and method are not clearly explained. I think the current version cannot be published.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
